text:
jack.support: Heads-up — we're getting a spike of 502s hitting hosted-api edge right now (12:03-12:12 UTC window). Multiple customers streaming requests fail with upstream resets. request_ids: f2a3c4 / b9e8d7 in traces.

anjali.sre: Can you paste one of the trace IDs and a short curl repro? Also any recent infra deploys?

jack.support: trace f2a3c4 shows upstream reset on h2 connection, envoy upstream response: "RST_STREAM". Quick log snippet:```
[2026-03-16T12:04:21Z] EDGE: conn reset from upstream=10.0.12.34:8080 id=f2a3c4 proto=h2 cause=WINDOW_UPDATE_ERROR
[2026-03-16T12:04:21Z] PROXY: 502 returning to client id=usr-482 auth=ok route=hosted-api
```

ben.ingress: I pushed a config tweak earlier to reduce per-upstream connection window (experiment for long-lived embeddings). That could explain WINDOW_UPDATE errors. I rolled it back at 12:05 but spike persists.

maria.ops: Noted customer escalations: 3 P1 tickets opened, one customer is on a live demo. We need a short customer-facing ETA.

ingress-bot: deploy "ingress-config/2026-03-16/conn-window-experiment" rolled back by ben.ingress at 2026-03-16T12:05:12Z (status: success).

anjali.sre: Repro steps request — trying to reproduce with streaming payloads. jack.support can you run this against the ingress LB and paste curl?

jack.support: Repro I used (simulates chunked streaming):

```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" --http2 \ 
  -X POST https://api.hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"stream":true,"input":"hello"}' --no-buffer
```

When I run it concurrently ~30 streams from a small vm it triggers resets in ~30-60s. Single requests succeed.

anjali.sre: Can you attach a full envoy log for one of the failures (include upstream host, local addr, and stream id)? Need to check conn pool exhaustion vs flow control runtime.

jack.support: Pasted a trimmed envoy log to the thread (link): https://internal-logs/redwood/ingress/f2a3c4.log — shows repeated `send WINDOW_UPDATE on closed stream` and `reset_due_to_connect_error`.

ben.ingress: From the logs it looks like two things: (1) small conn window change increased sensitivity to bursty streaming, (2) upstream auth-proxy occasionally takes longer during token refresh and holds streams open (backpressure). Combined -> conn pool stalls -> envoy resets idle streams -> 502.

maria.ops: Immediate mitigations?

anjali.sre: Short-term: 1) route affected host header -> warmdedicated pool (less multiplexing) 2) increase `upstream_connection_pool_size` and bump keepalive timeouts 3) enable per-route `max_concurrent_streams` guard to reduce head-of-line.

ben.ingress: I can push a temporary override to increase upstream conn window and bump max concurrent streams for hosted-api route. Will monitor. Pushing in 2 mins.

deploy-bot: Override config applied: ingress/hosted-api/conn-window-bump at 2026-03-16T12:07:40Z (targeted to pods: 6).

jack.support: After override - errors dropped from ~18% -> ~2% in last 3m for the affected cluster. Still monitoring.

maria.ops: Great. Please draft short status blurb for customers: one-liner cause + mitigation + ETA for root cause. I'll post to the P1 threads.

anjali.sre: Next steps: - run increased load test with streaming (30-100 concurrent) against canary ingress - correlate with auth-proxy traces to see token refresh latencies - add circuit-breaker fallback to spawn new upstream connection if stream stalls >10s.

ben.ingress: Will coordinate with auth team to see auth-proxy token refresh patterns. Sending logs to auth team now.

jack.support: Customer update posted. Tickets updated with workaround (we routed them to dedicated pool). Customers ack'd, one asked for retro.

maria.ops: @anjali.sre @ben.ingress assign owners for postmortem. Keep thread updated. :thumbsup:

anjali.sre: I'll own the action item for flow-control tuning and the postmortem. Ben — please attach the config diffs you pushed.

ben.ingress: Diff attached to the incident. I'll join the postmortem call.

jack.support: Thanks all — will close the customer escalations once postmortem doc links are in the ticket.
